subject.title: ci(windows): add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should the Windows smoke lane protect formatter/docs-command changes by expanding `runWindows` scope, or should the command set be narrowed or deferred?
rationale: The patch changes recurring CI behavior and runner cost, while the current scope does not cover the docs formatter path that motivated the smoke command.

options.title: Expand Scope And Keep Both Commands
options.body: Add the relevant docs formatter/doc-check surfaces to the Windows scope, keep both smoke commands, and require native PowerShell proof before merge.

options.title: Start With A Narrower Smoke
options.body: Limit the new Windows smoke to commands whose trigger scope and passing proof are already clear, then expand later.

options.title: Pause The CI Expansion
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and defer this recurring Windows smoke until maintainers choose the command set and runner budget.

recommendation.title: Expand Scope And Keep Both Commands
recommendation.body: Add the relevant docs formatter/doc-check surfaces to the Windows scope, keep both smoke commands, and require native PowerShell proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily concerns CI workflow scope and runner behavior, where this person has recent current-main history.
